The assignments are incredibly time-consuming. Each homework report is at least 50 pages long and since there is no way to completely check your answers, until the grades are announced (which takes a long time as the reports are very very long) you have no way of knowing whether your answers were correct. So, same mistakes can be repeated after each homework or quiz. The solution keys being posted after the assignments would be very helpful. The slides and lecture notes being posted on moodle before classes would also be incredibly helpful as it is hard to take notes without having the images shown on the slides. If you have no interest in the topic the lectures are very hard to follow as the topics are not similar to anything else we have seen in other classes. While EEE473 is not a prerequisite for the class, as someone who took 475 without taking 473, the concepts are quite hard to understand with no prior information. Taking 473 or 474 before would significantly change the outcome of this course.

She doesn't try to teach how to become an engineer. This is one of the first courses we take under EEE. This is the course that should make us start thinking as an engineer. This is not a physics class which tells us how things work under some circumstances. But she just tells how things work and how to calculate them. Yes it's very important to know these but it's more important to know what to do when we come across a problem. Yes I now learnt how to calculate everything about a bandpass filter. However if I come across a situation where it requires a band pass filter, I won't even have a guess what the bandwidth should be. Or what the filter's attenuation should be. I don't even have an idea where we use the power gain of a filter. Should we use impedance matching filters as well? Why does filters have a load? Cant we put an Opamp at the end of the filter and adjust the gain as we like? How do we find the output load of a given power source? I know how to calculate some values given some other values but that doesn't mean that I can actually design an analog circuit given them. And this isn't a negative aspect of the course but the instructor. This is something that can be explained in a matter of minutes. She could give real life examples and solve from the scratch but she decides to calculate TRC10's crystal filters. Half of the lectures are only equations on the board but not a bit intuition. We just memorize how to solve problems. It just feels like studying to university enterance exam.
